prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single nucleobases in DNA

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the clearest example on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists everywhere make bonds. The decisive idea, bulky electron-rich ligands that make oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination work for a very wide substrate range, is conceptually simple and chemically new. It is visible in countless syntheses, in medicinal and process chemistry and in materials. More than 25 years of independent use means the question of reproducibility is closed. Attribution is clean at two names, Buchwald and Hartwig, who developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled reactions and the mechanistic picture. Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precursor that belongs in the citation context, not in the laureate set. I pair it with base editing because colleagues across the table rank B058 highly, and the chemical content is real: a nucleobase deaminase tethered to a nicking Cas protein, with directed evolution of an adenine deaminase, converting one base to another without a double-strand break. Liu is the intellectual driver, and a single name keeps the union at three.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection to B030 is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize: some will see it as the same chemistry with a different heteroatom. My answer is that the C-N problem needed a new ligand concept and a separate mechanism, but I accept that the committee may weigh it as an extension. The strongest objection to B058 is that it sits at the border with biology and follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely, so the chemical novelty has to be argued, and clinical outcomes are still maturing. Pairing two unrelated achievements also dilutes the citation, and a prize for one coherent method would be tidier.

responses.point: Base editing is a chemist's contribution through evolved deaminases and is cleanest as a Liu-only or Liu-led prize, with therapeutic base editors already in patients.
responses.response: I agree that Liu alone is the cleanest attribution, and the union limit also pushes me there. I would not credit Komor and Gaudelli here even though they carried out the experiments, because it is a trainee-inclusion judgment we cannot defend for B058 and then refuse elsewhere. Where we differ is weight. I read B058 as the better second part of a shared prize rather than a stand-alone first choice, because the question of what is new beyond the 2020 CRISPR recognition has to be answered with the deaminase engineering and not with the clinical story.

responses.point: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible; Kosugi's tin-amine coupling is a precursor to be mentioned in the citation context rather than as a third laureate.
responses.response: I agree, and it matches my own opening. Kosugi coupled aminostannanes, which needed stoichiometric tin reagents, whereas the Buchwald and Hartwig reactions use free amines with a base and a general ligand-controlled cycle. That difference is the invention, so it is a case of precedent rather than co-discovery. I still want the committee to test the priority record and the Migita-type precedents before we settle, since you and I are the only two who ranked this first and our colleagues have not yet engaged with it.

responses.point: Induced degradation turns ubiquitin-proteasome proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, a general tool for removing proteins, with the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism supplying the chemical logic.
responses.response: I take the point that degraders are a real design principle with drug-discovery impact, and I keep B008 as my first alternative. My reservation is attribution and timing. Eight credited names compress into three laureates, PROTACs and molecular glues are partly separate stories (Crews and Deshaies versus Handa and Ito, with Ciulli's VHL ligands between), and there is still no approved PROTAC. If the committee wants a degrader prize, I would press for it to be defined as one of the two strands, not a loose composite.

responses.point: Liquid-liquid phase separation is a physical-chemical organising principle that reduces a messy cell-biological phenomenon to general thermodynamics.
responses.response: The concept is influential and I do not dispute the thermodynamic framing. My difficulty is the question I ask of every border-field candidate: what was new chemically? Polymer demixing is old, and the claim that many cellular condensates are genuinely liquid-like is still debated, partly because of overexpression artefacts. The attribution cut among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag also leaves out theorists. I would want the in vivo evidence to settle before this earns a prize, so I place it behind the synthetic and enabling-method candidates.

uncertainties: Whether the committee sees C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether Kosugi's priority should be recognised beyond the citation context, and who holds the first general catalytic claim.
Whether base editing differs enough chemically from the 2020 CRISPR recognition, and whether Liu alone is acceptable given Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida.
Whether a prize pairing two unrelated achievements would be preferred to a single coherent topic.
The final shape of any degrader prize: which of PROTAC and molecular-glue strands, and who is named.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the shortlisted candidates is a known Lund, KTH or Chalmers colleague, or my mentor Masamune. Buchwald and Hartwig work in my own area of synthetic methodology, which is a scientific closeness, not a personal or institutional tie.
